hiring.title: Hiring
hiring.intro: Student research opportunities and guidance for prospective collaborators.
hiring.welcome: I welcome inquiries from students interested in explainable AI, continual learning, and AI for space weather. Advertised positions and their application instructions are listed below.
hiring.phd_empty: There are currently no advertised openings for PhD students. For an independent project inquiry, please follow the guidance below.
hiring.undergraduate_empty: There are currently no advertised openings for undergraduate researchers. For an independent project inquiry, please follow the guidance below.
hiring.inquiry_intro: If no suitable position is advertised, you may still write to discuss a potential research collaboration. Please include:
hiring.proposal_guidance: A concise research proposal summary describing the project you would like to work on together: the research question, why it matters, your proposed approach, and how it connects to my research.
hiring.cv_guidance: A detailed CV including your education, relevant coursework, technical skills, research or project experience, and publications or portfolio links, if available.
hiring.availability_guidance: Your current degree level and availability, including when you hope to begin.
hiring.inquiry_note: Use the subject line “HUMAN INQUIRY — PhD” or “HUMAN INQUIRY — Undergraduate.” An inquiry is an expression of interest; it does not imply that a funded position is available.
hiring.inquiry_link: Email your proposal summary and CV
hiring.notice_heading: Your AI is not applying. You are.
hiring.notice_intro: A quick note before you reach out: I am interested in the person behind the application. Ideally, that person is also the one who wrote it.
hiring.notice_email: If an AI has read my papers, developed a profound passion for my research, and emailed me on your behalf, congratulations to the AI. I still need to hear from you. Please write a specific, personal message that tells me what actually interests you.
hiring.notice_cv: Listing Python, deep learning, and twelve other skills on a CV is remarkably easy. Explaining what you built with them takes a little more preparation. Please list experience you actually have, describe your own contribution, and be ready to discuss it. A small, honest project tells me more than an impressive fictional one.
hiring.notice_closing: AI tools can be useful. Borrowed enthusiasm, invented experience, and answers you cannot explain are less useful ways to begin a research relationship. Bring your curiosity, your questions, and your actual skills. That is a much better starting point.
